text:
alice: Heads-up — after the autoscaler downsize last night some GPU batch jobs started failing with connection errors. Observed: headless service `gpu-workers.prod` returns empty endpoints intermittently. Anyone else seeing this?

ben: Yeah I saw that too. Ran `kubectl get endpointslices -n prod | grep gpu-workers` and saw slices with 0 endpoints on a couple controller caches. Example output:
```
NAME                        AGE   ENDPOINTS   PORTS
gpu-workers-abcde           12m   0           9000/TCP
gpu-workers-fghij           11m   2           9000/TCP
```

carla: CoreDNS logs around the time show repeated NXDOMAIN/no endpoints for SRV lookups for the headless service:
```
[ERROR] plugin/route: no endpoints for service "gpu-workers.prod.svc.cluster.local"
[WARN] query: "_http._tcp.gpu-workers.prod.svc.cluster.local IN SRV" class IN
```

devops-bot: autoscaler:scaledown node-spot-3 (eu-west-1) at 2026-03-18T02:34:11Z

dave: My hypothesis: controller/endpoint-slice reconciliation lag after node drain + kube-proxy cleanup leaves some kube-proxy instances with stale rules, and CoreDNS caches the empty response briefly. Check kube-proxy logs and conntrack on the drained node.

alice: Confirmed `kubectl get endpoints -n prod gpu-workers` shows subsets missing for some selectors. Also noticed kube-proxy on node-spot-3 entered CrashLoopBackOff during the drain: `kubectl describe pod -n kube-system kube-proxy-node-spot-3` shows repeated failures on startup while trying to restore iptables/ipvs rules.

ben: Quick mitigation that helped in prod: 1) restarted coredns pods 2) restarted kube-proxy daemonset on the affected node(s). Restarting coredns made clients see endpoints again immediately (probably flushing the cache), but the root cause remained.

carla: For completeness, endpoint-slice controller logs show slow resyncs, e.g. `resync loop took 4m, targets 10m`, so during a burst of node removals it may not reconcile fast enough.

alice: Proposed immediate runbook:
- uncordon one recently-drained node to allow endpoints to reappear
- restart kube-proxy on nodes with stale rules (`kubectl rollout restart daemonset/kube-proxy -n kube-system --field-selector spec.nodeName=node-...`)
- restart coredns if cache seems stale (`kubectl rollout restart deployment/coredns -n kube-system`)

ben: +1. Also let's add an autoscaler pre-check that waits for endpointSlice stabilization for services with headless selectors before evicting a node. Small e2e to simulate downscale should catch this.

dave: Long term fixes to investigate: lower endpoint-slice controller resyncPeriod, improve immediate reconciliation after node deletion, and ensure kube-proxy startup tolerates rapid iptables/ipvs transitions. Also tune conntrack GC: scale-down spikes created a lot of conntrack entries that stalled connections.

carla: I'll draft a short playbook entry with the exact commands and the logs we collected, and open a PR to add the e2e scale-down test.

alice: I'll schedule a maintenance window to bump the autoscaler delay to 90s and roll kube-proxy/coredns next weekday. No objections? :thumbsup:

ben: tagging @infra-oncall in case we hit this during the next autoscale: `@infra-oncall`

devops-bot: Created incident INC-2026-042 and pinged infra-oncall.

infra-oncall: Acknowledged. Will monitor the next scale cycle and run the playbook if we see a recurrence.

carla: Putting links in the runbook: `kubectl get endpointslices -n prod -l app=gpu-workers -o wide`, `kubectl logs -n kube-system deployment/coredns --since=15m`, `sudo conntrack -L | grep node-spot-3` and the temporary heal commands.

alice: Thanks all — keeping this thread open until autoscaler change is in staging and we've got the e2e.
